issues.description: The problem statement and the template declare Course.instructor as a String, but the solution implementation declares the instructor property as an array of String ([String]). This type mismatch for the same attribute will confuse students about the intended type and causes disagreement between the specification/template and the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of Course.instructor consistent across all artifacts. Either change the problem statement and template to require instructor: [String] (and update documentation/examples), or modify the solution to use instructor: String (and update any code that treats it as an array). Preferably align the solution to instructor: String to match the problem text and the template.

issues.description: Inside the solution repository, Client.swift constructs a Course using a String for the instructor parameter, but Course.init in the solution expects an array of String ([String]). This constructor/parameter mismatch within the solution artifacts will not compile and is inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter types consistent within the solution. Either update Client.swift to pass an array of instructor names ([String]) to match Course.init, or change Course.init to accept a single String for instructor and update its property type accordingly. Ensure all solution files compile together and reflect the intended type.
